examples.ko: 신청서 맨 아래에 기타 질문을 적는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: At the bottom of the application there is a space to write other questions.
Please write any other comments below.
Enter your name, age and other information.

examples.ko: 안내문에 사과, 배, 기타 과일이라고 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The notice says apples, pears and other fruit.
You have to pay other costs separately.

examples.ko: 설문 항목 중에서 기타를 고르면 직접 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you choose Other in the survey options, you can write your own answer.

explain: 서류, 설문, 안내문에서 'A, B, 기타'처럼 나열한 것 뒤에 '그 밖의 것'을 모아 말할 때 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '그 밖에, 그 외에'라고 하는 편이 자연스러워요. 악기 '기타(guitar)'와 글자가 같아서 목록 속에 있으면 etc.예요.

phrases.example: 가방에는 책, 노트, 기타 등등이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: The bag has books, notebooks, and so on in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몇 가지를 말한 뒤 나머지를 줄여서 말할 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to sum up the rest of a list after naming a few items.

explain_en: It is common in forms, surveys and notices, after a list such as 'A, B, 기타', to gather everything else. When speaking, '그 밖에' or '그 외에' sounds more natural. It is spelled like 기타 (guitar), so inside a list it means etc.

examples.ko: 여름에는 저녁 일곱 시가 넘어서 해가 져요.
examples.en: In summer the sun sets after seven in the evening.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 해가 일찍 져서 금방 어두워져요.
examples.en: In winter the sun sets early, so it gets dark quickly.

examples.ko: 벚꽃이 다 지기 전에 같이 보러 가요.
examples.en: Let's go see the cherry blossoms together before they all fall.
The wind is blowing and the petals are falling.
When the sun sets, it gets a little cooler outside.
The rose that bloomed yesterday has already withered and fallen.

explain: 해와 달, 꽃이 '지다'이고 반대말은 '뜨다'(해, 달), '피다'(꽃)예요. '해가 저물다'도 비슷하지만 '저물다'는 '날이 저물다'처럼 하루가 끝나 갈 때도 쓰는 말이에요. '졌어요'는 '게임에서 지다'와 모양이 같으니 주어를 보세요.

phrases.en: Please come back home before the sun sets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저녁에 해가 서쪽으로 넘어갈 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sun goes down in the evening.

explain_en: The sun, moon and flowers '지다', and the opposites are '뜨다' (sun, moon) and '피다' (flowers). '해가 저물다' is similar, but '저물다' also describes a day coming to an end, as in '날이 저물다'. '졌어요' also looks like 'lost a game', so check the subject.

en: to be full; to be filled

examples.en: The bus is full of people.
The stadium was filled with cheering people.

examples.ko: 컵에 물이 다 차면 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me when the cup is full of water.

examples.ko: 가방이 책으로 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The bag is so packed with books that I can't fit any more.
The seats are not all filled yet.
It's the day the house gets filled with guests.

explain: '가득 차다'처럼 쓰고 반대는 '비다'예요. 상태를 말할 때는 '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 '자리가 꽉 차 있어요'처럼 말해요. 누가 채우는 거면 '채우다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I ran up the stairs, so I'm out of breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달리거나 계단을 오른 뒤처럼 숨을 쉬기가 힘들 때 써요. '숨이 차다'는 한 덩어리로 외워 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is hard to breathe, such as after running or climbing stairs. Memorize '숨이 차다' as one set phrase.

explain_en: It is used as in '가득 차다', and the opposite is '비다'. To describe a state, people add '-아/어 있다', as in '자리가 꽉 차 있어요'. If someone is doing the filling, use '채우다'.

examples.en: The pool water is too cold today.
My feet are cold, so I can't fall asleep.
The wind is cold today, so dress warmly.
If I drink cold water, my teeth hurt.
If the floor is cold, wear thick socks.

examples.ko: 손이 차지 않아요? 제 장갑 빌려 드릴까요?
examples.en: Aren't your hands cold? Shall I lend you my gloves?

explain: 손, 물, 바닥처럼 닿았을 때 차가운 것에 써요. 날씨나 방 안이 추울 때는 '춥다'가 더 자연스러워요. '찬 물'처럼 관형형이 '찬'이 되고, 반대말은 '뜨겁다'나 '따뜻하다'예요.

phrases.en: My hands get cold in winter, so I wear gloves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이 만져 보면 차가울 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one's hands feel cold to the touch.

explain_en: It is used for things that feel cold to the touch, such as hands, water and floors. For cold weather or a cold room, '춥다' sounds more natural. The modifier form is '찬', as in '찬 물', and the opposites are '뜨겁다' and '따뜻하다'.
